title: Paella Valenciana
subtitle: Spanish saffron rice with chicken and rabbit
excerpt: The original paella from Valencia: chicken and rabbit cooked with short-grain rice, saffron, and green beans in a wide pan until the rice forms a golden crust at the base. Cooked over an open fire in its homeland, achievable in a wide pan on a hob.

recipe.sourceNotes: Paella Valenciana is the original paella, from the Albufera region south of Valencia. The dish takes its name from the wide, shallow pan (la paella or la paellera) it is cooked in. The classic Valencian recipe contains chicken, rabbit, ferraura (flat green beans), garrofón (large white beans), tomato, saffron, paprika, rosemary, and short-grain rice (specifically bomba, senia, or bahía. The socarrat (crisp caramelised rice crust at the base) is considered the mark of a well-made paella and is achieved by increasing the heat in the final minutes of cooking without stirring.

recipeTools.notes: A 40 to 46 cm paella pan or the widest frying pan available.

content.text: Once the rice goes in, do not stir: stirring releases starch and prevents the socarrat from forming. The rice-to-stock ratio is critical: use the correct amount and do not add more liquid once the rice is in. The socarrat forms in the last 2 to 3 minutes when you increase the heat slightly and let the rice dry out and begin to crisp at the base. Listen for a faint crackling sound: that is the socarrat forming. Test by sliding a spoon under the rice at the edge: it should lift away in one piece.

items.preparation: trimmed and cut into 5 cm lengths
steeped in 100 ml hot stock for 10 minutes

content.text: Heat the oil in the paella pan over medium-high heat. Season and brown the chicken pieces all over for 8 to 10 minutes. Push to the edges. Fry the green beans in the centre for 3 minutes. Push to the edges.

Add the garlic and paprika to the centre and stir for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until reduced. Pour in the hot stock and saffron. Add the rosemary sprigs. Season. Bring to a rapid boil.

Pour in the rice evenly across the pan. Do not stir after this point. Cook at a lively simmer for 10 minutes. Reduce to medium-low and cook for a further 8 to 10 minutes until the stock is absorbed and the rice is just tender.
Increase the heat to medium-high for the last 2 minutes to form the socarrat. Listen for crackling. Remove from the heat and rest for 5 minutes. Serve from the pan with lemon wedges.
